item.title: How I Studied Go at Night and Built an AI Interview Trainer: Voice Input, Spaced Repetition, and Docker in Production
item.description:
Hi Habr! For the last six months, I've been trying to break into backend development with Go. By day, I tinker with cars in an auto repair shop, and by night, I sit at my computer trying to digest the runtime, scheduler, and memory management. At some point, there were just too many topics: slice headers, Swiss Tables, GMP, escape analysis. Simply reading endless notes and articles on the go wasn't very effective – everything quickly evaporated from my mind, and I was afraid to go to real interviews due to a lack of confidence in the fundamentals. I didn't want to create another To-Do list or a blog clone, so I decided to build a tool for myself: a Telegram bot that quizzes me on technical questions, evaluates my answers (text and voice) by strict criteria, and makes me repeat topics I struggled with. Ultimately, the project grew into a working service on a server. Below, I'll explain how I built the backend and what pitfalls I encountered along the way. Read more

item.title: Why One Large Model Won't Replace an OCR Pipeline: RWB Content Moderation Experience
item.description:
Large Vision-Language Models (VLMs) are getting good at reading text from images. So why does Wildberries' content moderation process still use a seven-stage OCR pipeline for millions of product cards daily, instead of a single model? This article delves into the reasons behind this choice, sharing RWB's experience in building and maintaining a robust OCR system.

item.title: Virtual Employees and Agents at the "Russian Tech 2" Meetup
item.description:
Many have their local harness set up, others work in the cloud. What if you deploy a harness for a large company? What to do if you have to wait almost 40 seconds for the first agent response? What can be optimized and what will it lead to? Okay, deployed and optimized, but how to make agents work with employees? And how to assess the business impact of AI implementation? I haven't set up my harness yet, and I was interested in seeing the experience of other companies. So I went to the MWS meetup on this topic. First, they told the history of AI agents and the basics: what is the wrapper around the model. Then there was a report on optimization: at MWS, everything is deployed on Kubernetes and supports OpenClaw and Hermes simultaneously. Then, heads of departments discussed how agents work with employees. Finally, there was a report on implementing AI in organizations and assessing its impact. Read more

item.title: Qwen4-Max-Preview is out
item.description:
Qwen4-Max-Preview is Alibaba's new flagship model, released on November 11, 2026, as a preview. Access is available through various Qwen platforms. Token-based payments are not yet implemented. The Personal Lite subscription costs $6/month, with a limited-time offer for new users at $3 (until November 30). The subscription includes 20,000 credits per month, with consumption varying by model, token count, reasoning mode, and tool calls. During the preview, credit consumption for this model is significantly reduced (up to 80% discount), with an even steeper discount (up to 92%) during off-peak hours in Beijing time (10 PM to 8 AM). The preview ends on November 25, after which the model will be disabled. Alibaba has not announced a full release date. Read more

item.title: 1,674,813 Tokens in a Single Request: How I Cleaned Up OpenWebUI Context and Then Moved the Agent Outside
item.description:
Input tokens exceed 922,000 tokens. Your messages resulted in 1,674,813 tokens — this error kicked off a story that spanned six months. We have a self-hosted OpenWebUI with an internal assistant for a small team: files, documents, and minor engineering tasks. Initially, I wrote a filter to clean up tool results from the history. Then I realized I was patching the wrong place and moved agent execution to a separate service using OpenAI Agents SDK and Codex SDK. Along the way, I also stumbled upon the streaming Responses API. Read more

item.title: How We Removed Humans from Code Review (But Not Everywhere Yet)
item.description:
Hello Habr! My name is Anna Sabotovich, and I lead the implementation of an AI reviewer in the Garage Eight product group. The most frequent question I get is: 'So, when will it replace humans?' I'll answer right away: for some code, it already has. In October, our iOS teams removed the third mandatory approval for merge requests (MRs). Now, in product repositories, there are no more than two. Meanwhile, in the reviewer's repository, 35 MRs were merged in October, and only six had approval from someone other than the author. In the internal development analytics service, 69 MRs were merged, and none had approval from another person: the author merges themselves. I want to share how we learned to trust AI and what we plan to do next. Read more

item.title: How I'm Developing a System That Doesn't Take AI Agents at Their Word
item.description:
An AI agent can figure out how a website works, find a bug, and suggest a reasonable fix. But what if the solution is technically correct, but the user authorized something else entirely? Who should verify the agent's actions before they become real changes? In the first article, I explained how I gave an AI agent access to MODX via MCP, and in the second, how we organized its independent work with live websites. By then, a decent infrastructure had already emerged around MCP: file operations, locks, backups, change history, and browser checks. Read the third part
